findings.evidence: content/quantum-observable-universe/braids-and-knots/reducible-reps.md:3 — root-of-unity construction used without explicit regime declaration — The PBW filtration on $\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2))$ equips the associated graded algebra $\mathrm{gr}\mathcal{U}_q$ with a commutative product. The leading monomials of the $q$-Serre relations provide non-overlapping obstructions whose resolution yields a normal-form basis coinciding with the Lusztig divided-power basis. In positive characteristic, this construction produces the distribution algebra $\mathrm{Dist}(G)$ of the lifted formal group $G$ as a deformation of the commutative $\mathrm{Dist}(H)$. The strong multiplicativity condition guarantees that the Frobenius relation is preserved at every filtration degree.

findings.evidence: content/quantum-observable-universe/lifting-and-descent/direct-limit-lusztig.md:1 — root-of-unity construction used without explicit regime declaration — We explicitly realise the algebra $\mathcal{A}_\infty$ ([direct limit algebra](#def:direct-limit-algebra)) as the Lusztig integral form of the quantised enveloping algebra $\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2))$ \[lusztig1993]. At each level $n$, we obtain the fibre algebra $\mathrm{SU}_{q_n}(2)$ by specialising the $\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}]$-form $\mathcal{U}^{\mathbb{Z}}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2))$ ([substrate parameter](#def:substrate-parameter)) along $q \mapsto q_n \in k^{\times}$. The direct limit inherits the divided power basis $(E^{(m)}, F^{(m)}, K^{\pm 1})$ from the integral form. This ensures that the quaternionic jet embedding ([quaternionic spectral resolvents](#def:quaternionic-spectral-resolvents)) remains robust under the arithmetic :refterm[descent]{#descent} to $M_0$. The $q$-deformed scaling function $\exp_q(r) - 1$ (equation [eq:q-exp](#eq:q-exp)) regulates the transition between the divided power bases of the space-like and time-like resolvents.

findings.label: sec:direct-limit-intro
findings.evidence: content/quantum-observable-universe/lifting-and-descent/direct-limit-intro.md:3 — root-of-unity construction used without explicit regime declaration — We define the direct limit algebra $\mathcal{A}_\infty = \varinjlim_n \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n)$. In the smooth case, this recovers $\varinjlim \Gamma(J^1\mathcal{S}_n, \mathrm{SU}_{q_n}(2))$. We interpret this colimit through three lenses: Lusztig's integral form, the profinite jet shell, and Yekutieli's twisted-deformation stack. We then identify the unique $G_q$-invariant vacuum state functional on $\mathcal{A}_\infty$. Twisted quantization glues the local algebras globally across the tower via the obstruction class. The admissible Gröbner-style ordering lifts to the colimit, providing the well-founded order essential for downstream sections.

findings.label: sec:jones-polynomials
findings.evidence: content/quantum-observable-universe/models-of-qous/jones-polynomials.md:3 — root-of-unity construction used without explicit regime declaration — The fusion category $\mathrm{Rep}_{\mathbb{F}_p}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2))$ carries a canonical $R$-matrix. This arises from the universal $R$-matrix of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ specialised at a primitive $\ell$-th root of unity in $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$. This $R$-matrix promotes the fundamental representation $V$ to a braided object. The braid group $B_n$ acts on $V^{\otimes n}$. The Markov trace then produces a knot invariant. Following standard Reshetikhin–Turaev normalisation, this yields the Jones polynomial $J_K(q) \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}]$ modulo $p$.
